wc.heading: Company DIO · DSO · DPO · CCC
wc.desc: DIO from uploaded SKU inventory & COGS, covered rows only. DSO / DPO from the period's trial-balance context. CCC is a company roll-up, not per-SKU.
wc.infoAria: What do DIO, DSO, DPO and CCC mean?
wc.dioNoInputs: Inventory / COGS not provided on any SKU
wc.dioFormulaWeighted: weighted by Inventory (per-SKU DIO; COGS not persisted)
wc.dioMissingHint: Add Inventory value and COGS columns to the upload to compute DIO.
wc.noTrialBalance: no trial balance in this session
wc.dsoMissingHint: Load a period with a trial balance to compute DSO.
wc.dpoMissingHint: Load a period with a trial balance to compute DPO.
wc.cccHint: CCC is computed only when DIO, DSO and DPO are all available.
wc.modalDesc: What each pill measures and where the number comes from.
wc.dioBody: How many days, on average, stock sits before it sells — sum(Inventory) ÷ sum(COGS) × 365 across covered SKUs. Lower is leaner; a high DIO means cash is tied up in shelves and warehouses.
wc.dsoBody: How many days it takes to collect cash after a sale — receivables relative to revenue, read from the loaded period's trial balance. Lower means customers pay faster.
wc.dpoBody: How many days you take to pay suppliers — payables relative to COGS, from the trial balance. Higher means you hold onto cash longer (as long as it doesn't strain supplier terms).
wc.cccBody: The net days your cash is locked in operations — DIO + DSO − DPO, at the company level. It's the headline: how long from paying for inventory to collecting from customers. Lower (or negative) is stronger working-capital health.

concepts.revenue: Everything you billed customers this period, before costs.
concepts.operating_revenue: All income from the day-to-day business, including other operating income.
concepts.net_turnover: Sales of goods and services, net of discounts given.
concepts.cogs: What the goods you sold cost you to buy or make.
concepts.gross_profit: Sales minus the direct cost of what you sold.
concepts.operating_expenses: Everything running the business costs — salaries, rent, services, materials.
concepts.opex: Everything running the business costs — salaries, rent, services, materials.
concepts.ebit: Profit from operations, before interest and tax.
concepts.ebitda: Operating profit before interest, tax and depreciation — a proxy for cash generated.
concepts.depreciation_amortization: The yearly wear-and-tear cost of equipment and other long-lived assets.
concepts.depreciation: The yearly wear-and-tear cost of equipment and other long-lived assets.
concepts.net_financial_result: Financial income minus financial costs — interest, FX and the like.
concepts.income_tax: Tax owed on this period's profit.
concepts.net_profit: What's left after every cost, interest and tax — the bottom line.
concepts.net_income: What's left after every cost, interest and tax — the bottom line.
concepts.total_assets: Everything the company owns, valued in money.
concepts.current_assets: Assets that turn into cash within a year — stock, receivables, cash.
concepts.cash: Money available right now in bank accounts and petty cash.
concepts.inventory: Stock waiting to be sold — raw materials, work in progress, finished goods.
concepts.receivables: Money customers owe you for what you've already delivered.
concepts.ppe: Long-life physical assets — land, buildings, machines, vehicles.
concepts.current_liabilities: Bills due within a year — suppliers, salaries, taxes, short-term loans.
concepts.accounts_payable: Money you owe suppliers for what you've already received.
concepts.short_term_debt: Bank borrowings due within the next 12 months.
concepts.long_term_debt: Bank loans and leases due after more than a year.
concepts.total_debt: All the money borrowed from banks and lenders, short and long term.
concepts.shareholders_equity: The owners' stake — what remains after all debts are paid.
concepts.total_equity: The owners' stake — what remains after all debts are paid.
concepts.operating_cash_flow: Cash the day-to-day business actually generated this period.
concepts.capex: Cash spent on equipment, buildings and other long-term assets.
concepts.free_cash_flow: Cash left after operations and investment — free to repay debt or pay dividends.
concepts.enterprise_value: What the whole business is worth, debt included.
concepts.equity_value: What the owners' share of the business is worth.
concepts.ebitda_margin: EBITDA as a share of sales — how profitable the operations are.
concepts.ebit_margin: Operating profit as a share of sales.
concepts.net_margin: How much of each sale ends up as final profit.
concepts.gross_margin: What's left of sales after direct costs, as a percentage.
concepts.gross_margin_ratio: What's left of sales after direct costs, as a percentage.
concepts.current_ratio: Can short-term assets cover short-term bills? Above 1 means yes.
concepts.quick_ratio: Like the current ratio, but without counting stock you'd first have to sell.
concepts.cash_ratio: How much of the short-term bills you could pay with cash on hand today.
concepts.net_debt_ebitda: Roughly how many years of EBITDA it would take to repay net debt.
concepts.debt_to_equity: How much debt the company uses for every leu of owners' money.
concepts.equity_ratio: The share of assets financed by owners rather than debt.
concepts.debt_to_assets: The share of assets financed with borrowed money.
concepts.roe: Profit earned for every leu the owners have invested.
concepts.roa: How efficiently the company's assets generate profit.
concepts.ev_ebitda_multiple: The valuation multiple: business value divided by EBITDA.
concepts.open_risks: Findings flagged critical or high in this period's analysis.
concepts.open_opportunities: Improvement ideas surfaced by this period's analysis.

pl.reconNote: Operational net profit ({{amount}} {{currency}}) is the headline figure across this report. Account 722 is a non-cash credit that capitalizes internally-incurred costs into CIP (account 231); the offsetting cost sits inside account 628 (third-party services). Net P&L effect of the 722/628 wash is ~zero; statutory ct 121 is shown above as the reconciled total — not as a competing headline.

footnote.ownWorkTitle: Account 722 (Capitalized own work) — {{amount}} {{currency}} is not external revenue.
footnote.ownWorkBody: It is the credit-side offset that capitalizes internally-incurred construction costs into CIP (account 231 — YTD movement matches 722 exactly). The corresponding cost is sitting inside 628 Other third-party services ({{ext}}). Net P&L effect: ~zero. For a "clean" operating view, strip both: revenue drops to ~{{revenue}}, opex drops to ~{{opex}}, clean EBITDA ≈ {{ebitda}}.
footnote.rentalTitle: Real cash-generative operating revenue is essentially just rental income (706): {{amount}} {{currency}}.
footnote.rentalBody: Against that base, the underlying property-management EBITDA is the more meaningful number.
